title: Mobile SDK: resilient offline trace delivery and context stitching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Mobile clients frequently experience intermittent connectivity and process restarts that break end-to-end tracing. Current SDK instrumentation drops spans when the app is offline or relies on best-effort delivery that causes large gaps in trace graphs. This initiative adds an on-device, encrypted persistent span queue with robust delivery, sequence ids for stitching across sessions, and server-side reconciliation hooks so traces remain useful for latency and error analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mobile SDK enqueues spans/events reliably across app restarts and survives process kill. 2) Enqueued spans are encrypted at rest and delivered in ordered batches when connectivity is available. 3) Server accepts batched spans and uses sequence id + client session id to stitch with upstream requests; end-to-end trace continuity is demonstrable in Console for a simulated offline-to-online scenario. 4) Metrics emitted: queued_spans_gauge, queued_bytes_gauge, delivery_success_counter, delivery_failure_counter, last_delivery_latency_ms. 5) Feature flag to opt-out at build/runtime and telemetry disabled for regulatory customers.
technical_decisions: - Persist queue as an append-only SQLite table with write-ahead logging for durability; small entries are snappy-compressed to limit storage. - Each span is augmented with a client_session_id and monotonic sequence_id assigned by SDK; sequence windowing allows server to detect missing ranges and request partial replays. - Delivery uses exponential backoff + jitter with max batch size 100 spans or 256KB. - Use existing /ingest/batched-traces endpoint with a new header X-Client-Context for session metadata; server-side reconciler component will join client batches with request-origin traces via trace_id and session hints. - Encryption uses platform KMS wrappers (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain) and falls back to ephemeral encryption when unavailable; telemetry path logs only counts, never raw spans, until server verifies consent. - To limit on-device cost we cap local queue at 10MB by default and evict oldest non-critical spans beyond that unless user consents.
open_questions: - Edge case: how to handle multi-process apps that share the same SDK store? Proposed: use file locks and process-scoped sequence windows. - Should SDK request token renewal be piggybacked on delivery calls? (Pros: reduces extra calls; Cons: increases coupling). - Privacy: explicit opt-in for high-fidelity request body capture; default is headers + coarse metadata. - Platform limits: confirm iOS background upload window (connectivity deferrals) — may need OS-specific retry heuristics.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha K: Initial spike complete. Verified append-only SQLite strategy holds under 5k small spans in emulator. Disk usage ~4.2MB for 3k spans. Created PoC and basic delivery loop.

2026-03-04 - Liam O: Reviewed PoC. Asked to replace custom crypto with platform KMS wrappers. Raised concern about sequence_id overflow for long-running sessions; recommending 64-bit monotonic counter with wrap detection.

2026-03-06 - Aisha K: Implemented encryption using Android Keystore / iOS Keychain helpers. Added batch size cap and health metric for queue depth. Started end-to-end test harness that simulates airplane mode toggles.
2026-03-08 - PM review (Jorge M): Confirmed compliance requirement: for EU-regulated customers the default must be opt-out for payload capture. Added release flag and updated docs.

2026-03-10 - Eng infra (Nina P): Server reconciler endpoint implemented in PR #14567; needs contract doc for X-Client-Context header format and error codes for partial-accept. Action: finalize header schema and add integration tests.

2026-03-11 - QA (Rina S): Running flaky test: delivery sometimes times out on low bandwidth emulated networks. Proposed increasing delivery timeout and capturing last error code in delivery_failure_counter labels.

2026-03-12 - Liam O: Marking core work done; remaining tasks: finalize e2e tests, add canary on dev console, and add observability dashboards (queued spans heatmap, delivery latency percentile) before close.
